source: Written for this app, from the titles/captions/hashtags section of a user-supplied pet-comedy series brief. NOT AI Video Bootcamp course material. The course's own publishing advice is transcribed in ugc_bank.json's `publishing` block and is quoted below where the two disagree.
note: The first thing in this app that writes words for a PLATFORM rather than for a model. It is deterministic like every other tool here - it composes from patterns and the story's own captions rather than calling a language model - and it is gated by social_lint.py, because a generator with nothing deciding whether its output is good is the one thing this project does not ship.

hashtag_conflict.note: The two sources disagree, and this bank records both rather than quietly picking one. The series brief asks for 15-20 hashtags per post. This app's own ugc_bank.json, transcribed from the AI Video Bootcamp, says the opposite: 'Four at most. More than that and the algorithm gets a confused signal about the topic.' social_lint enforces the BRIEF's range, because that is what was asked for. The course's advice is not deleted - it ships as `course_advice` below and is printed by build_social.py on every run.
hashtag_conflict.course_advice: Four at most. More than that and the algorithm gets a confused signal about the topic.

title_patterns: {premise_short} - and then the paw came down
caption_patterns: Every single day with this one. {premise_sentence} Tell me your cat does this too.
{premise_sentence} The face afterwards is what gets me every time.
Parenting a toddler and parenting this cat are the same job. {premise_sentence}
{premise_sentence} He was not sorry. He is never sorry.

hashtags.note: Three tiers, drawn in order until the count is met: `core` always, then `niche`, then `broad`. Tiering rather than one flat list so the first tags - the ones that carry the most weight - are the ones that actually describe the video.

banned_claims.note: Words that turn a joke caption into a claim somebody could act on, or into bait a platform demotes. Short and concrete on purpose - this is not a tone police.
